policy_text:
Ostrava-Lune Foundation, Halbrecht Early Inquiry Grants: eligibility rules (2027 cycle)
An application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. The project period, from start date to end date, may not exceed 39 weeks.
R2. Applications hosted by a teaching hospital may budget at most $5,000 for travel.
R3. The lead applicant must have received a doctorate no more than 6 years before 2027. This rule does not apply if the applicant has a documented Corran career break and the doctorate is at most 10 years old.
R4. The application must include a letter of support from the host. This rule does not apply if the host is a university, whose standing agreement with the foundation replaces the letter.
R5. If the type of host institution is not stated, treat the host as an independent institute.
R6. Research with human participants requires approval from the Mereth ethics board.
R7. If ethics approval is not mentioned, assume none was obtained.
R8. Equipment and travel together may not exceed $30,000.
R9. The host institution must be a university, a teaching hospital or a community laboratory.

An application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. The project period, from start date to end date, may not exceed 39 weeks.
R2. Applications hosted by a teaching hospital may budget at most $5,000 for travel.
R3. The lead applicant must have received a doctorate no more than 6 years before 2027. This rule does not apply if the applicant has a documented Corran career break and the doctorate is at most 10 years old.
R4. The application must include a letter of support from the host. This rule does not apply if the host is a university, whose standing agreement with the foundation replaces the letter.
R5. If the type of host institution is not stated, treat the host as an independent institute.
R6. Research with human participants requires approval from the Mereth ethics board.
R7. If ethics approval is not mentioned, assume none was obtained.
R8. Equipment and travel together may not exceed $30,000.
R9. The host institution must be a university, a teaching hospital or a community laboratory.

The lead applicant's doctoral degree was conferred in 2020, per the attached transcript. The title of the project was shortened at the suggestion of the host's grants office. Travel is budgeted at $10,000. Equipment and travel together come to $30,000. The work plan covers a project period of 28 weeks. Several figures in the narrative were drawn by a graduate student. The host's research dean wrote a letter of support for the application. The applicant has not applied to the Mereth ethics board. The work involves no human participants. No Corran career break form was submitted. The project is scheduled to begin on February 15, 2027. No open data plan accompanies the proposal.

fact_labels.pi_years_since_phd: years since the lead applicant's doctorate (counted to 2027)
fact_labels.letter_of_support: letter of support from the host
fact_labels.ethics_approval: ethics approval from the Mereth board

rules.text: The project period, from start date to end date, may not exceed 39 weeks.
Equipment and travel together may not exceed $30,000.
Applications hosted by a teaching hospital may budget at most $5,000 for travel.
The application must include a letter of support from the host. This rule does not apply if the host is a university, whose standing agreement with the foundation replaces the letter.
Research with human participants requires approval from the Mereth ethics board.
The host institution must be a university, an independent institute or a teaching hospital.
If the type of host institution is not stated, treat the host as an independent institute.
The lead applicant must have received a doctorate no more than 8 years before 2027, unless the applicant has a documented Corran career break and the doctorate is at most 10 years old.
If ethics approval is not mentioned, assume none was obtained.

policy_text:
City of Marrowgate, Bureau of Street Apparatus: temporary equipment placement permits
A permit is approved only if the application meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. In a residential zone, equipment may weigh no more than 4 tonnes.
R2. Night work requires a crew of at least 6.
R3. If an application does not mention night work, assume all work is in daytime hours.
R4. The application must be filed at least 7 days before placement begins.
R5. No work may take place between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.. This rule does not apply if the site lies outside a residential zone.
R6. Tessel-type crawler cranes may not be placed on city streets. This rule does not apply if liability insurance covers at least $3,000,000.
R7. Equipment may stay in place for at most 35 days, counted from the start date to the removal date.
R8. If the zoning of the site is not stated, treat the site as residential.
R9. Equipment may weigh no more than 8000 kg. This rule does not apply if the operator holds a Ferrin certificate at level 4 or higher and the equipment weighs at most 10000 kg.

The applicant asked whether the permit fee can be paid in two parts.
The application was filed on March 8, 2027.
The applicant intends to set up a Class K-2 skylift on the street.
The previous tenant of the building ran a bicycle shop.

The crew numbers 10.
Liability insurance covers $0.
The equipment would stay in place for 28 days.
The manufacturer sheet gives an operating weight of 2,000 kilograms.
A nearby cafe owner called the bureau to ask about parking.
The site lies in a commercial district, not a residential zone.
The equipment is due to arrive on site on April 19, 2027.

The applicant expects to clear the site by May 17, 2027. No sidewalk closure is requested. Notice letters went out to every neighbouring address. The named operator holds a Ferrin certificate at level 1. The crew numbers 10. Liability insurance covers $0. The manufacturer sheet gives an operating weight of 2,000 kilograms. A nearby cafe owner called the bureau to ask about parking. The site lies in a commercial district, not a residential zone. The equipment is due to arrive on site on April 19, 2027.

A permit is approved only if the application meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. In a residential zone, equipment may weigh no more than 4 tonnes.
R2. Night work requires a crew of at least 6.
R3. If an application does not mention night work, assume all work is in daytime hours.
R4. The application must be filed at least 7 days before placement begins.
R5. No work may take place between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.. This rule does not apply if the site lies outside a residential zone.
R6. Tessel-type crawler cranes may not be placed on city streets. This rule does not apply if liability insurance covers at least $3,000,000.
R7. Equipment may stay in place for at most 35 days, counted from the start date to the removal date.
R8. If the zoning of the site is not stated, treat the site as residential.
R9. Equipment may weigh no more than 8000 kg. This rule does not apply if the operator holds a Ferrin certificate at level 4 or higher and the equipment weighs at most 10000 kg.

A permit is approved only if the application meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. Tessel-type crawler cranes may not be placed on city streets, unless liability insurance covers at least $3,000,000.
R2. In a residential zone, equipment may weigh no more than 4 tonnes.
R3. If an application does not mention night work, assume all work is in daytime hours.
R4. The application must be filed at least 7 days before placement begins.
R5. No work may take place between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m., unless the site lies outside a residential zone.
R6. If the zoning of the site is not stated, treat the site as residential.
R7. Night work requires a crew of at least 6.
R8. Equipment may weigh no more than 8000 kg, unless the operator holds a Ferrin certificate at level 3 or higher and the equipment weighs at most 10000 kg.
R9. Equipment may stay in place for at most 21 days, counted from the start date to the removal date.

A permit is approved only if the application meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. Tessel-type crawler cranes may not be placed on city streets, unless liability insurance covers at least $3,000,000.
R2. In a residential zone, equipment may weigh no more than 4 tonnes.
R3. If an application does not mention night work, assume all work is in daytime hours.
R4. The application must be filed at least 7 days before placement begins.
R5. No work may take place between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m., unless the site lies outside a residential zone.
R6. If the zoning of the site is not stated, treat the site as residential.
R7. Night work requires a crew of at least 6.
R8. Equipment may weigh no more than 8000 kg, unless the operator holds a Ferrin certificate at level 3 or higher and the equipment weighs at most 10000 kg.
R9. Equipment may stay in place for at most 21 days, counted from the start date to the removal date.

R1. If an application does not mention night work, assume all work is in daytime hours.
R2. If a sidewalk will be closed, all neighbouring addresses must have been notified in writing.
R3. In a residential zone, equipment may weigh no more than 4 tonnes.
R4. No work may take place between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m..
R5. Equipment may weigh no more than 6000 kg, unless the operator holds a Ferrin certificate at level 4 or higher and the equipment weighs at most 8000 kg.
R6. Liability insurance must cover at least $2,000,000. This rule does not apply if the equipment is a Class K-1 skylift.
R7. Night work requires a crew of at least 4.
R8. The application must be filed at least 7 days before placement begins.
R9. The operator must hold a Ferrin certificate at level 1 or higher, unless the equipment is a Class K-1 skylift.
R10. If an application does not mention notifying neighbours, assume they were not notified.

A permit is approved only if the application meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. If an application does not mention notifying neighbours, assume they were not notified.
R2. The operator must hold a Ferrin certificate at level 2 or higher. This rule does not apply if the equipment is a Class K-1 skylift.
R3. The application must be filed at least 14 days before placement begins.
R4. In a residential zone, equipment may weigh no more than 6 tonnes.
R5. If an application does not mention night work, assume all work is in daytime hours.
R6. Equipment may weigh no more than 8000 kg, unless the operator holds a Ferrin certificate at level 4 or higher and the equipment weighs at most 10000 kg.
R7. Night work requires a crew of at least 6.
R8. If a sidewalk will be closed, all neighbouring addresses must have been notified in writing.
R9. Liability insurance must cover at least $1,500,000. This rule does not apply if the equipment is a Class K-1 skylift.
R10. No work may take place between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m..

policy_text:
Protocol VX-118 (celvorex in Tarrant fibrosis): enrollment criteria
A participant is enrolled (approved) only if every criterion below is met. Criteria marked as defaults say what to assume when the screening record is silent on a point.

R1. The PRX-7 serum level must be at least 200 ng/mL. This rule does not apply if the Kelman index is 8 or higher.
R2. At least 6 weeks must have passed since the last systemic therapy.
R3. If the site tier is not recorded, treat the site as tier B.
R4. Participants must be between 25 and 65 years old inclusive.
R5. Screening must take place on or after the consent date and no more than 21 days after it.
R6. Tier C Halvard sites may only enroll participants aged 55 or younger.
R7. Participants on an anticoagulant must have a resting heart rate of at most 75 beats per minute.
R8. Participants taking an anticoagulant are excluded, unless they enroll at a tier A Halvard site, where coagulation is monitored weekly.
R9. The Kelman fibrosis index may not exceed 10.

R1. The PRX-7 serum level must be at least 200 ng/mL. This rule does not apply if the Kelman index is 8 or higher.
R2. At least 6 weeks must have passed since the last systemic therapy.
R3. If the site tier is not recorded, treat the site as tier B.
R4. Participants must be between 25 and 65 years old inclusive.
R5. Screening must take place on or after the consent date and no more than 21 days after it.
R6. Tier C Halvard sites may only enroll participants aged 55 or younger.
R7. Participants on an anticoagulant must have a resting heart rate of at most 75 beats per minute.
R8. Participants taking an anticoagulant are excluded, unless they enroll at a tier A Halvard site, where coagulation is monitored weekly.
R9. The Kelman fibrosis index may not exceed 10.

The enrolling site is a tier B Halvard site. Renal function testing gave a creatinine clearance of 30 mL/min. The participant is 70 years old. The pulse at rest measured 105. Imaging gave a Kelman index of 10. There is no history of major bleeding. The PRX-7 serum level came back at 250 ng/mL. There is no record of prior celvorex exposure. The visit started thirty minutes late because of a scheduling mix-up. A family member accompanied the participant to the visit. The intake form was completed on a tablet in the waiting room. The participant works as a piano tuner.

The participant drove two hours to reach the clinic. The participant was once hospitalized for a major bleed. Screening was completed on February 1, 2027. Renal function testing gave a creatinine clearance of 60 mL/min. Informed consent was signed on February 1, 2027. A translator was offered but not needed. The participant received celvorex in an earlier study. It has been 16 weeks since the participant's last dose of systemic therapy. The participant is 60 years old. The visit started thirty minutes late because of a scheduling mix-up. A family member accompanied the participant to the visit.

rules.text: Tier C Halvard sites may only enroll participants aged 55 or younger.
The PRX-7 serum level must be at least 150 ng/mL. This rule does not apply if the Kelman index is 10 or higher.
At least 8 weeks must have passed since the last systemic therapy.
Participants must be between 25 and 65 years old inclusive.
Participants taking an anticoagulant are excluded.
The Halden composite score (PRX-7 level in ng/mL plus ten times the Kelman index) may not exceed 350.
Participants previously exposed to celvorex are excluded.
Screening must take place on or after the consent date and no more than 21 days after it.
If the site tier is not recorded, treat the site as tier B.
If the record does not mention bleeding, assume no history of major bleeding.
Creatinine clearance must be at least 75 mL/min, unless the participant is enrolled at a tier A Halvard site and creatinine clearance is at least 60 mL/min.
Participants on an anticoagulant must have no history of major bleeding.

policy_text:
Twelfth Symposium on Quorian Methods (SQM 2027): submission and review policy
A submission is admitted to review with its assigned reviewer (approved) only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the submission record is silent on a point.

R1. The main text and references together may not exceed 11 pages.
R2. Supplementary material may not exceed 50 MB. This rule does not apply if the paper is in the Applied Quorian track, which allows up to 100 MB.
R3. Applied Quorian track papers may use at most 3 pages of references.
R4. Submissions must be uploaded no later than April 17, 2027, unless the chairs granted an extension and the paper was uploaded by April 21, 2027.
R5. The assigned reviewer may not work at the same institution as any author, unless the paper is in the Position Paper track, which is reviewed openly by the whole committee.
R6. The assigned reviewer may not have co-authored a paper with any author within 365 days before the submission date.
R7. Papers reporting studies with human participants must include an ethics statement. This rule does not apply if the paper is in the Position Paper track.
R8. Any supplementary material must be anonymized.
R9. If the record does not say whether supplementary material is anonymized, treat it as not anonymized.
R10. Papers uploaded under a deadline extension may not exceed 7 pages of main text.
R11. If the record does not mention an ethics statement, assume there is none.
